title: An AI Cracked an 80-Year-Old Math Problem
hook: An OpenAI model produced a solution to a famous math problem that had stumped people for about 80 years — a real milestone, with some important fine print.
key_points: An OpenAI model generated a solution to a long-unsolved famous math problem.
The problem had reportedly gone unsolved by humans for roughly 80 years.
A machine writing a proof still needs human mathematicians to verify it's correct.
It's a striking result, not proof that AI now 'does math' on its own across the board.
content_html: In June 2026, Ars Technica reported that an OpenAI model produced a solution to a famous math problem that had reportedly gone unsolved for around 80 years. That's a genuinely notable moment: it's the kind of hard, long-open question that has resisted plenty of smart human effort. The honest takeaway, though, sits between two extremes — it's neither a parlor trick nor a sign that machines have suddenly mastered mathematics.
extra_html: A couple of caveats keep this in proportion. First, a proof written by an AI is a claim until human mathematicians check every step; verification is what turns a generated answer into an accepted result. Second, solving one celebrated problem doesn't mean AI now "does math" reliably on its own — these systems can still stumble on far simpler arithmetic, and a single success doesn't generalize to everything. So enjoy the milestone for what it is: an impressive, specific achievement that experts will scrutinize, not a blanket guarantee about machine reasoning.

flashcards.explanation_html: One striking solution to one problem is a milestone, not evidence that AI handles all of mathematics independently.
